sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about Silbo Gomero: a whistled language from La Gomera (one of the Canary Islands — mountainous terrain). Silbo can convey complex messages, not just simple ones. Brain study showed silbadores (Silbo speakers) and non-whistlers produced different results. The Guanches (original inhabitants) introduced Silbo; the Spanish adopted it in the 15th century. No precise data on number of whistle languages worldwide. Children in La Gomera now learn Silbo in school. How it works: high- and low-frequency tones represent different vowels/consonants in Spanish; pitch controlled using the tongue/finger; volume changed with cupped hand. Used by shepherds and isolated communities; transmits brief messages in daily use; can relay emergency information e.g. about accidents. Future threatened by mobile phones; Canaries authorities seeking UNESCO heritage status.]

passage.title: The ethics of being a consumer

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about big businesses, environmental damage, and consumer power: many big businesses harm people/environment with no moral standards; lack of control by governments and public involvement leads to problems like flooding/overfishing/destruction of trees. The public/consumers can prevent environmental damage by individual action. Ways the public can influence businesses: boycotts, selective purchasing, pressure groups, shareholder power. BSE example: a fast-food company forced their meat suppliers to follow the law rather than meat packers persuading government to reduce expenses. The writer argues consumers can influence businesses; public has done so before; writer believes it is important to distinguish acceptable from unacceptable behaviour; questions whether businesses will show more concern for environment in future.]
